# layout.target-size — Touch target is smaller than the 24×24 CSS px minimum

- **Check ID:** `layout.target-size`
- **Default severity:** `warning`; users can override it in `seaworthy.config.json`.
- **Needs:** `html`, `browser` (only with `--rendered`)
- **Standards:** WCAG 2.5.8
- **Source module:** `packages/verify/src/checks/touch-target.ts`
- **Prose page:** [`docs/checks/layout.target-size.md`](../layout.target-size.md) — embedded below verbatim; write it there, never here.

A rendered interactive element — link, button, form control, or ARIA widget — whose box is smaller than the 24×24 CSS px minimum of WCAG 2.5.8.

## Why it matters

Small touch targets are the classic mobile failure: a person with limited fine motor control, someone using a phone on a moving train, and an agent driving a browser through coordinates all miss targets under 24×24 CSS px and hit whatever sits beside them. The target may work with a mouse, which is exactly why a parser-only review misses it: whether a control is 20 px or 44 px is decided by the CSS box model and the viewport, not by the markup.

## What it checks

Every interactive element (`a[href]`, `area[href]`, `button`, `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `summary`, and elements with a `button`, `link`, `checkbox`, `radio`, `switch`, `tab`, or `menuitem` role) is measured with its rendered bounding box on every page, at each shared width — phone (375 px), tablet (768 px), and desktop (1280 px). A box strictly smaller than 24×24 CSS px is a finding naming the element's CSS selector, a snippet, its smallest measured size, and the widths it was under the minimum at; one element is one finding even when every width fails.

These are never reported:

- **Inline links inside a sentence.** WCAG 2.5.8 exempts targets displayed inline within a flow of text: the link's computed display is `inline` and its nearest block-level ancestor holds prose around the link's own words. A standalone link with no words beside it is a control, not a sentence, and stays measured.
- **Targets of exactly 24×24**, which meet the minimum.
- **Disabled controls** (`disabled`) and **invisible elements** (`display: none`, `visibility: hidden`, or a zero-area box).
- **Elements off screen**: boxes entirely outside the rendered viewport, including the `-9999px` trick, are not tap targets where the person taps.

This check needs a browser and is opt-in: it runs only under `--rendered` (see [ADR 0005](../adr/0005-headless-browser.md)). Pages load from `file://` URLs and requests to remote `http(s)` resources are aborted, so a rendered run stays offline; there is no broken fixture for it for the same reason.

The boundary with [`a11y.axe`](a11y.axe.md): axe-core ships its own `target-size` rule for the same success criterion. This check owns touch-target **size** — it is deterministic, its message carries the measured box, and it applies the inline exception explicitly — so axe's `target-size` rule is switched off in a11y.axe's covered-rule table and one small target is never reported twice. axe keeps `target-offset`, the WCAG 2.5.8 **spacing** rule (targets that crowd each other), which this check does not measure.

Deliberately not modelled are the criterion's other exceptions — a user-agent-supplied control, an equivalent target elsewhere on the page, or the same function served by a larger target — so a small icon button that duplicates a larger text button is still reported; fix the duplicate or the size.

## How to fix

Give the control a rendered box of at least 24×24 CSS px. Change the source, not the built file:

```html
<!-- before: a 20×20 icon button, under the WCAG 2.5.8 minimum -->
<button class="icon-button" aria-label="Close">✕</button>
<!-- after: min-width/min-height keep the visible box small but the tap area legal -->
<style>.icon-button { min-width: 24px; min-height: 24px; }</style>
<button class="icon-button" aria-label="Close">✕</button>
```

For inline links in navigation that are not part of a sentence, padding is the usual fix:

```css
/* before: a 40×16 px nav link */
.nav a { padding: 0; }
/* after: 40×24 px rendered box */
.nav a { padding: 4px 0; }
```

## Options

None. The 24 CSS px minimum is the AA success criterion and is not configurable; the severity is, as for every check, through `checks."layout.target-size".severity`.

## Standards

- [WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html)
